key_insight: A feature-based reduced-order manifold can replace POD modes to model transient bluff-body wakes under arbitrary time-varying actuation with an interpretable analytical dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This provides a control-oriented surrogate for actuated wakes that can predict response without requiring unsteady training data, making it useful for flow control design.
method: Replace POD modes with a feature-based manifold of the same dimension.
Build the state space from dynamic features that encode coherent-structure evolution.
Augment the state with transient actuation-response terms to obtain simple analytical dynamics.
evidence_signal: The model is validated on the fluidic pinball at Re=30 across several representative actuation scenarios and is reported to accurately reproduce transient dynamics.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on a canonical low-Reynolds-number configuration, so generalization to more complex or higher-Re flows still needs careful validation.
paper_title: Feature-based manifold model of actuated wakes
